subject: Art & Design
title: Poster Design: A Century of Visual Impact
description: A 60-second lesson on Poster Design: A Century of Visual Impact.

hook.text: Toulouse-Lautrec's Moulin Rouge poster (1891) turned advertising into art. The street became a gallery.

buildup.text: Posters combine image, text, and composition into one instant message. They must work at a glance.

discovery.text: WWI and WWII propaganda posters (Uncle Sam, Rosie the Riveter) proved design's power to mobilize nations.

twist.text: Psychedelic 1960s concert posters broke every design rule: illegible text, clashing colors. And they worked perfectly.

climax.text: Today's best posters still follow the same principle: one idea, maximum impact, zero explanation needed.

punchline.text: A great poster says everything in three seconds or less.

quiz.question: What principle makes poster design effective?
options: One clear idea with maximum impact that needs no explanation
Including as much text as possible

details.summary: Poster design has evolved from Toulouse-Lautrec's 1890s lithographs through Art Nouveau, Bauhaus, psychedelic 1960s, and punk's DIY aesthetic to today's digital formats. The poster remains graphic design's purest challenge: communicate a complete message to a passing viewer in seconds.
details.whyItMatters: Posters distill all design principles into a single surface — hierarchy, contrast, color, typography, and imagery must work together instantly. Studying poster history is studying the evolution of visual communication itself.
takeaways: Posters must communicate a complete message in seconds
The medium evolved through Art Nouveau, Bauhaus, and punk
Poster design distills all graphic design principles at once

faq.question: What makes the Bauhaus posters still feel modern?
faq.answer: Bauhaus designers eliminated ornamentation, used geometric shapes, primary colors, and sans-serif type to create compositions of pure visual logic. This reductive approach — nothing decorative, everything functional — anticipated modern minimalist design by a century.

faq.question: Are physical posters still relevant in the digital age?
faq.answer: Yes. Posters work in public spaces where screens don't — bus stops, construction fences, community boards. Music and film posters remain cultural artifacts. And poster design principles apply directly to social media graphics, which are essentially digital posters designed for scrolling.
